text:
alex: FYI: us-west2 preemptible GPUs spiking interruptions this morning. We're seeing ~12% churn on spot node groups and the CA is doing extra churn. Thinking quick fixes: 1) faster fallback to on-demand/warm pool, 2) taint strategy so long-running model pods avoid spot, 3) lifecycle hook to avoid double-drain. Any quick wins?

maria: Quick wins that helped us before: label spot NGs with node.k8s.io/lifecycle=spot and taint spot=true:NoSchedule. Only give tolerations to burst/ephemeral pods. Use a high-priority PriorityClass for critical model-serving so they prefer on-demand NGs.

suresh: CA flags to check: `--expander=least-waste` and `--balance-similar-node-groups` to avoid overprovisioning similar types. Also bump `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to reduce aggressive scale-down during frequent preempts. Make sure `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false` so CA takes system pods into account.

olivia: We should also run a termination-notice handler daemonset that does: 1) detect termination notice, 2) cordon + annotate node, 3) wait a short window to let jobs checkpoint, 4) drain once. This prevents two controllers racing to drain the same node. Example handler (pseudo):

```
#!/bin/sh
if metadata_has_termination_notice; then
  kubectl annotate node $NODE preemptible=true --overwrite
  kubectl cordon $NODE
  sleep 10  # small buffer so pods can checkpoint
  kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
fi
```

k8s-ops: Also consider mixed-instance-type nodegroups (different GPU types) and spreading spot NGs across AZs to reduce correlated preemption. Keep a tiny warm pool of 1-2 on-demand GPUs per AZ to accept handoffs — might add a small baseline cost but saves deployment pain.

infra-bot: autoscaler: scaled up nodegroup gpu-spot-usw2b by 2 (reason: insufficient resources for pods labeled model/latency-critical) :rocket:

alex: Good notes. Plan: 1) add labels+taints to spot NGs, 2) update deployment tolerations for batch/evictable jobs only, 3) deploy termination handler DS + doc, 4) tweak CA flags and scale-down timeout. I'll open a PR with the daemonset and CA changes for review. Thanks all :clap:
